title.zh: 卷十四 志第四 禮樂四
title.raw: 卷十四 志第四 禮樂四 Volume 14 Treatises 4: Rites and Music 4

sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__其非常祀，天子有時而行之者，曰封禪、巡守、視學、耕藉、拜陵。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__As for extraordinary sacrifices, those the Son of Heaven performs at times, they are called feng and shan, imperial tours, school inspection, plowing the sacred field, and tomb worship.
translations.idiomatic: __FORCETOC__Among extraordinary sacrifices that the Son of Heaven performs only on occasion are the feng and shan rites, imperial tours of inspection, school visits, plowing the sacred field, and worship at imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 文中子曰：「封禪，非古也，其秦、漢之侈心乎？

translations.literal: Wang Tong said: "Feng and shan are not ancient; are they not the extravagant hearts of Qin and Han?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong said: "The feng and shan rites are not ancient custom; are they not the extravagant impulse of Qin and Han?"

sentences.zh: 」蓋其曠世不常行，而於禮無所本，故自漢以來，儒生學官論議不同，而至於不能決，則出於時君率意而行之爾。

translations.literal: " For they are performed only once in many ages and have no foundation in ritual; hence since Han, Confucian scholars and academic officials have debated differently and reached no decision, so they come down to whatever the ruler of the time wills.
translations.idiomatic: " They are performed only once in many generations and rest on no canonical ritual foundation; since the Han, Confucian scholars and court academicians have argued without agreement, and in the end each age's ruler has simply carried them out as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝嘗令牛弘、辛彥之等撰定儀注，為壇泰山下，設祭如南郊而已，未嘗升山也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui once ordered Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, and others to draft ritual regulations, setting up an altar below Mount Tai and performing sacrifice like the southern suburb only, never ascending the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui once ordered Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, and others to draft ritual protocols: an altar was built below Mount Tai and sacrifice performed like the southern suburban rite, but the emperor never climbed the mountain.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗已平突厥，而年穀屢豐，羣臣請封泰山。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang had already pacified the Turks, and the harvests were repeatedly abundant; the ministers requested feng on Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizong of Tang had pacified the Turks and harvests were repeatedly abundant, his ministers petitioned for a feng rite on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 太宗初頗非之，已而遣中書侍郎杜正倫行太山上七十二君壇迹，以是歲兩河大水而止。

translations.literal: Taizong at first strongly opposed it; later he sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Du Zhenglun to trace on the mountain the altars of the seventy-two lords, but stopped because that year the two Yellow River regions suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong at first strongly opposed the idea; later he sent Vice Director of the Secretariat Du Zhenglun to survey on the mountain the traces of the seventy-two lords' altars, but the plan was dropped when both Yellow River regions suffered major floods that year.

sentences.zh: 其後羣臣言封禪者多，乃命祕書少監顏師古、諫議大夫朱子奢等集當時名儒博士雜議，不能決。

translations.literal: Afterward many ministers spoke of feng and shan; he then ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu, Remonstrance Grandee Zhu Zishe, and others to gather the famous Confucians and erudite doctors of the time for mixed discussion, but no decision could be reached.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, as more ministers urged feng and shan, he ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu, Remonstrance Grandee Zhu Zishe, and others to convene leading Confucians and court erudites for joint debate, yet still no conclusion could be reached.

sentences.zh: 於是左僕射房玄齡、特進魏徵、中書令楊師道博採眾議奏上之，其議曰：「為壇於泰山下，祀昊天上帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling, Special Advance Wei Zheng, and Secretariat Director Yang Shidao broadly collected the various opinions and memorialized them; their proposal said: "Set up an altar below Mount Tai and sacrifice to August Heaven the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Left Vice Director Fang Xuanling, Special Advance Wei Zheng, and Secretariat Director Yang Shidao gathered the various opinions and submitted a memorial; their proposal read: "Establish an altar below Mount Tai and sacrifice to August Heaven the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 壇之廣十二丈，高丈二尺。

translations.literal: The altar twelve zhang wide and one zhang two chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The altar should be twelve zhang wide and one zhang two chi high.

sentences.zh: 玉牒長一尺三寸，廣、厚五寸。

translations.literal: The jade tablet one chi three cun long, five cun wide and thick.
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet one chi three cun long, five cun in width and thickness.

sentences.zh: 玉檢如之，厚減三寸。

translations.literal: The jade cover like it, three cun less in thickness.
translations.idiomatic: The jade cover the same dimensions, three cun less in thickness.

sentences.zh: 其印齒如璽，纏以金繩五周。

translations.literal: Its seal teeth like a seal, bound with gold cord five rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Its seal teeth like an imperial seal, wrapped with gold cord in five rounds.

sentences.zh: 玉策四，皆長一尺三寸，廣寸五分，厚五分，每策皆五簡，聯以金。

translations.literal: Four jade slips, all one chi three cun long, one cun five fen wide, five fen thick; each slip five tablets, linked with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Four jade slips, each one chi three cun long, one cun five fen wide, and five fen thick; each slip comprised five tablets joined with gold.

sentences.zh: 昊天上帝配以太祖，皇地祇配以高祖。

translations.literal: August Heaven the Supreme Lord was associated with the Grand Ancestor; August Earth the Earthly Lord with the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven the Supreme Lord was paired with the Grand Ancestor; August Earth the Earthly Lord with the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 已祀而歸格于廟，盛以金匱。

translations.literal: After sacrifice they returned and lodged in the temple, stored in a gold casket.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice they returned and lodged the offerings in the ancestral temple, stored in a gold casket.

sentences.zh: 匱高六寸，廣足容之，制如表函，纏以金繩，封以金泥，印以受命之璽。

translations.literal: The casket six cun high, wide enough to hold them, shaped like a memorial case, bound with gold cord, sealed with gold mud, stamped with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The casket was six cun high and wide enough to contain them, shaped like a memorial case, bound with gold cord, sealed with gold mud, and stamped with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 而玉牒藏于山上，以方石三枚為再累，纏以金繩，封以石泥，印以受命之璽。

translations.literal: The jade tablet was stored on the mountain, with three square stones as a double pile, bound with gold cord, sealed with stone mud, stamped with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet was stored on the mountain within a double pile of three square stones, bound with gold cord, sealed with stone mud, and stamped with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 其山上之圓壇，土以五色，高九尺，廣五丈，四面為一階。

translations.literal: The round altar on the mountain used the five colors of earth, nine chi high, five zhang wide, with one flight of steps on each side.
translations.idiomatic: The round altar on the mountain was built of earth in the five colors, nine chi high and five zhang wide, with one flight of steps on each side.

sentences.zh: 天子升自南階，而封玉牒。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ascended from the southern steps and sealed the jade tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven ascended from the southern steps and performed the sealing of the jade tablet.

sentences.zh: 已封，而加以土，築為封，高一丈二尺，廣二丈。

translations.literal: After sealing, earth was added and built into a mound one zhang two chi high and two zhang wide.
translations.idiomatic: After the sealing, earth was piled to form a mound one zhang two chi high and two zhang wide.

sentences.zh: 其禪社首亦如之。

translations.literal: The shan at Sheshou was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The shan rite at Sheshou followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 其石檢封以受命璽，而玉檢別製璽，方一寸二分，文如受命璽。

translations.literal: The stone cover was sealed with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate, while the jade cover had a separate seal made, one cun two fen square, with characters like the Seal of Receiving the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The stone cover was sealed with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate; the jade cover had a separate seal made, one cun two fen square, inscribed like the Seal of Receiving the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 以石距非經，不用。

translations.literal: Stone distance-blocks were deemed uncanonical and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Stone distance-blocks were deemed uncanonical and were not used.

sentences.zh: 又為告至壇，方八十一尺，高三尺，四出陛，以燔柴告至，望秩羣神。

translations.literal: They also made an Arrival Announcement altar, eighty-one chi square and three chi high, with steps on four sides, burning firewood to announce arrival and ranking the host of spirits by gaze.
translations.idiomatic: They also built an Arrival Announcement altar eighty-one chi square and three chi high, with steps on four sides, burning firewood to announce arrival and invoking the host of spirits by gaze.

sentences.zh: 」遂著于禮，其他降禪、朝覲皆不著。

translations.literal: " This was then written into the Rites; the descent-shan and court-audience portions were not written in.
translations.idiomatic: " This was then entered in the ritual code; the descent-shan and court-audience portions were not recorded.

sentences.zh: 至十五年，將東幸，行至洛陽，而彗星見，乃止。

translations.literal: By year fifteen, when he was about to travel east, he reached Luoyang and a comet appeared, so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifteenth year, as he prepared to travel east, he reached Luoyang; a comet appeared, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 高宗乾封元年，封泰山，為圓壇山南四里，如圓丘，三壝，壇上飾以青，四方如其色，號封祀壇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng under Gaozong, he performed feng on Mount Tai, setting a round altar four li south of the mountain like the Round Mound, with three enclosures; the altar top was adorned in blue and the four sides in their respective colors, named the Feng Sacrifice Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's first year of Qianfeng he performed the feng rite on Mount Tai, erecting a round altar four li south of the peak on the Round Mound model with three enclosures; the altar top was adorned in blue and the four sides in their respective colors, and it was named the Feng Sacrifice Altar.

sentences.zh: 玉策三，以玉為簡，長一尺二寸，廣一寸二分，厚三分，刻而金文。

translations.literal: Three jade slips, jade tablets one chi two cun long, one cun two fen wide, three fen thick, carved with gold script.
translations.idiomatic: Three jade slips fashioned as jade tablets one chi two cun long, one cun two fen wide, and three fen thick, carved with gold script.

sentences.zh: 玉匱一，長一尺三寸，以藏上帝之冊；

translations.literal: One jade casket, one chi three cun long, to store the Supreme Lord's register;
translations.idiomatic: One jade casket, one chi three cun long, to hold the Supreme Lord's register;

sentences.zh: 金匱二，以藏配帝之冊。

translations.literal: two gold caskets to store the associate lords' registers.
translations.idiomatic: two gold caskets to hold the associate lords' registers.

sentences.zh: 纏以金繩五周，金泥、玉璽，璽方一寸二分，文如受命璽。

translations.literal: Bound with gold cord five rounds, gold mud and jade seal; the seal one cun two fen square, with characters like the Seal of Receiving the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: All were bound with gold cord in five rounds, sealed with gold mud and a jade seal one cun two fen square, inscribed like the Seal of Receiving the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 石䃭以方石再累，皆方五尺，厚一尺，刻方其中以容玉匱。

translations.literal: Stone chests used square stones in double piles, each five chi square and one chi thick, hollowed square within to hold the jade casket.
translations.idiomatic: Stone chests were built of square stones in double piles, each pile five chi square and one chi thick, hollowed square within to receive the jade casket.

sentences.zh: 䃭旁施檢，刻深三寸三分，闊一尺，當繩刻深三分，闊一寸五分。

translations.literal: Beside the chest were set covers, carved three cun three fen deep and one chi wide; where the cord lay, carved three fen deep and one cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Covers were set beside each chest, carved three cun three fen deep and one chi wide; grooves for the cord were three fen deep and one cun five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 石檢十枚，以檢石䃭，皆長三尺，闊一尺，厚七分；

translations.literal: Ten stone covers to cover the stone chests, all three chi long, one chi wide, seven fen thick;
translations.idiomatic: Ten stone covers to cap the stone chests, each three chi long, one chi wide, and seven fen thick;

sentences.zh: 印齒三道，皆深四寸，當璽方五寸，當繩闊一寸五分。

translations.literal: three seal teeth, all four cun deep; where the seal lay, five chi square; where the cord lay, one cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: each with three seal teeth four cun deep; the seal seat five chi square; the cord groove one cun five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 檢立於䃭旁，南方、北方皆三，東方、西方皆二，去䃭隅皆一尺。

translations.literal: Covers stood beside the chests: three on south and north, two on east and west, each one chi from the chest corner.
translations.idiomatic: The covers stood beside the chests—three on the south and north, two on the east and west—each one chi from a chest corner.

sentences.zh: 䃭纏以金繩五周，封以石泥。

translations.literal: The chest was bound with gold cord five rounds and sealed with stone mud.
translations.idiomatic: Each chest was bound with gold cord in five rounds and sealed with stone mud.

sentences.zh: 距石十二，分距䃭隅，皆再累，皆闊二尺，長一丈，斜刻其首，令與䃭隅相應。

translations.literal: Twelve distance-stones, apportioned at the chest corners, all double piles, two chi wide and one zhang long, the heads cut slanting to match the chest corners.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve distance-stones placed at the chest corners, all in double piles two chi wide and one zhang long, their heads cut slanting to align with the chest corners.

sentences.zh: 又為壇於山上，廣五丈，高九尺，四出陛，一壝，號登封壇。

translations.literal: They also made an altar on the mountain, five zhang wide and nine chi high, with steps on four sides and one enclosure, named the Ascension Feng Altar.
translations.idiomatic: They also built an altar on the mountain five zhang wide and nine chi high, with steps on four sides and one enclosure, named the Ascension Feng Altar.

sentences.zh: 玉牒、玉檢、石䃭、石距、玉匱、石檢皆如之。

translations.literal: Jade tablet, jade cover, stone chest, stone distance, jade casket, and stone covers were all as above.
translations.idiomatic: Jade tablet, jade cover, stone chest, stone distance-blocks, jade casket, and stone covers all followed the same specifications.

sentences.zh: 為降禪壇於社首山上，八隅、一成、八陛如方丘，三壝。

translations.literal: A descent-shan altar was built on Mount Sheshou, eight corners, one tier, eight flights like the Square Mound, with three enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: A descent-shan altar was built on Mount Sheshou with eight corners, one tier, and eight flights like the Square Mound, with three enclosures.

sentences.zh: 上飾以黃，四方如其色，其餘皆如登封。

translations.literal: The top was adorned in yellow and the four sides in their colors; the rest all followed the Ascension Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Its top was adorned in yellow and the four sides in their respective colors; everything else followed the Ascension Feng rite.

sentences.zh: 其議略定，而天子詔曰：「古今之制，文質不同。

translations.literal: When the proposals were largely settled, the Son of Heaven issued an edict: "Rites ancient and modern differ in ornament and substance.
translations.idiomatic: When the proposals were largely settled, the Son of Heaven issued an edict: "Ancient and modern ritual forms differ in ornament and substance.

sentences.zh: 今封禪以玉牒、金繩，而瓦尊、匏爵、秸席，宜改從文。

translations.literal: Now feng and shan use jade tablets and gold cord, yet earthenware vessels, gourd cups, and straw mats should be changed to follow ornament.
translations.idiomatic: For feng and shan we now use jade tablets and gold cord, yet earthenware vessels, gourd cups, and straw mats should be upgraded to match the ceremony's dignity.

sentences.zh: 」於是昊天上帝褥以蒼，地祇褥以黃，配褥皆以紫，而尊爵亦更焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon August Heaven the Supreme Lord's cushion was blue-green, the Earthly Lord's yellow, associates' purple, and the vessels and cups were also changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon cushions for August Heaven the Supreme Lord were made blue-green, for the Earthly Lord yellow, for the associates purple, and the ritual vessels were changed as well.

sentences.zh: 是歲正月，天子祀昊天上帝于山下之封祀壇，以高祖、太宗配，如圓丘之禮。

translations.literal: In the first month of that year the Son of Heaven sacrificed to August Heaven the Supreme Lord at the Feng Sacrifice Altar below the mountain, with Gaozu and Taizong as associates, like the Round Mound rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of that year the Son of Heaven sacrificed to August Heaven the Supreme Lord at the Feng Sacrifice Altar below the mountain, with Gaozu and Taizong as associates, following Round Mound protocol.

sentences.zh: 親封玉冊，置石䃭，聚五色土封之，徑一丈二尺，高尺。

translations.literal: He personally sealed the jade register, placed it in the stone chest, and piled five-colored earth to seal it, one zhang two chi in diameter and one chi high.
translations.idiomatic: He personally sealed the jade register, placed it in the stone chest, and sealed it with piled five-colored earth one zhang two chi in diameter and one chi high.

sentences.zh: 已事，升山。

translations.literal: When finished, he ascended the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When that was done, he ascended the mountain.

sentences.zh: 明日，又封玉冊于登封壇。

translations.literal: The next day he again sealed a jade register at the Ascension Feng Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sealed another jade register at the Ascension Feng Altar.

sentences.zh: 又明日，祀皇地祇于社首山之降禪壇，如方丘之禮，以太穆皇后、文德皇后配，而以皇后武氏為亞獻，越國太妃燕氏為終獻，率六宮以登，其帷帟皆錦繡。

translations.literal: The day after, he sacrificed to August Earth the Earthly Lord at the descent-shan altar on Mount Sheshou like the Square Mound rite, with Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Wende as associates, while Empress Wu served as secondary offerer, Princess of Yue Yan as final offerer, leading the six palaces to ascend; all curtains were brocade and embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day he sacrificed to August Earth the Earthly Lord at the descent-shan altar on Mount Sheshou following Square Mound protocol, with the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Wende as associates; Empress Wu served as secondary offerer and Princess of Yue Yan as final offerer, leading the six palaces to ascend while all curtains were brocade and embroidery.

sentences.zh: 羣臣瞻望，多竊笑之，又明日，御朝覲壇以朝羣臣，如元日之禮。

translations.literal: The ministers gazed on and many secretly laughed; the next day he held court at the Audience Altar to receive the ministers, like New Year's rite.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers looked on and many secretly laughed; the next day he held court at the Audience Altar to receive the ministers, as on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 乃詔立登封、降禪、朝覲之碑，名封祀壇曰舞鶴臺，登封壇曰萬歲臺，降禪壇曰景雲臺，以紀瑞焉。

translations.literal: He then ordered steles for Ascension Feng, descent-shan, and audience erected, naming the Feng Sacrifice Altar Dancing Crane Terrace, the Ascension Feng Altar Long Live Terrace, and the descent-shan altar Jingyun Terrace, to record the auspices.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered steles erected for the Ascension Feng, descent-shan, and audience rites, naming the Feng Sacrifice Altar Dancing Crane Terrace, the Ascension Feng Altar Long Live Terrace, and the descent-shan altar Jingyun Terrace to commemorate the auspicious event.

sentences.zh: 其後將封嵩嶽，以吐蕃、突厥寇邊而止。

translations.literal: Afterward, when he was about to perform feng on Mount Song, it stopped because Tibetans and Turks raided the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he planned a feng rite on Mount Song, Tibetan and Turkic raids on the frontier forced cancellation.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年，又作奉天宮於嵩山南，遂幸焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun he again built Fengtian Palace south of Mount Song and then visited it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchun he built Fengtian Palace south of Mount Song and visited it.

sentences.zh: 將以明年十一月封禪，詔諸儒國子司業李行偉、考功員外郎賈大隱等草具其儀，已而遇疾，不克封，至武后遂登封焉。

translations.literal: He intended feng and shan in the eleventh month of the following year and ordered the Confucians Guozi Supervisor Li Xingwei, Investigation Bureau Outer Gentleman Jia Dayin, and others to draft the rites; he fell ill and could not perform feng; it was Empress Wu who later performed the ascent-feng.
translations.idiomatic: He planned feng and shan for the eleventh month of the following year and ordered Confucian officials including Guozi Supervisor Li Xingwei and Investigation Bureau Outer Gentleman Jia Dayin to draft the protocols; illness prevented the rite, and it was Empress Wu who later completed the ascent-feng.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元十二年，四方治定，歲屢豐稔，羣臣多言封禪，中書令張說又固請，乃下制以十三年有事泰山。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan under Xuanzong, the four quarters were settled and harvests repeatedly abundant; many ministers urged feng and shan, and Secretariat Director Zhang Yue again pressed firmly; an edict was issued that the thirteenth year would have business at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanzong's twelfth year of Kaiyuan the realm was settled and harvests repeatedly abundant; many ministers urged feng and shan, and Secretariat Director Zhang Yue pressed the matter again; an edict fixed the thirteenth year for the Mount Tai rites.

sentences.zh: 於是說與右散騎常侍徐堅、太常少卿韋縚、秘書少監康子元、國子博士侯行果刊定儀注。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue, with Right Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Xu Jian, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Chao, Vice Director of the Secretariat Kang Ziyuan, and Guozi Erudite Hou Xingguo, edited and fixed the ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue then joined Right Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Xu Jian, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Chao, Vice Director of the Secretariat Kang Ziyuan, and Guozi Erudite Hou Xingguo to revise and fix the ritual protocols.

sentences.zh: 立圓臺於山上，廣五丈，高九尺，土色各依其方。

translations.literal: A round terrace was set on the mountain, five zhang wide and nine chi high, earth colors each according to its direction.
translations.idiomatic: They erected a round terrace on the mountain five zhang wide and nine chi high, with earth colors according to each direction.

sentences.zh: 又於圓臺上起方壇，廣一丈二尺，高九尺，其壇臺四面為一階。

translations.literal: On the round terrace they raised a square altar one zhang two chi wide and nine chi high; the altar terrace had one flight of steps on each of four sides.
translations.idiomatic: On the round terrace they raised a square altar one zhang two chi wide and nine chi high, with one flight of steps on each side.

sentences.zh: 又積柴為燎壇於圓臺之東南，量地之宜，柴高一丈二尺，方一丈，開上，南出戶六尺。

translations.literal: They also piled firewood for a burning altar southeast of the round terrace, sized to the ground, firewood one zhang two chi high and one zhang square, open on top, with a six-chi door opening south.
translations.idiomatic: They also piled firewood for a burning altar southeast of the round terrace, sized to the terrain: the pyre one zhang two chi high and one zhang square, open on top with a six-chi opening facing south.

sentences.zh: 又為圓壇於山下，三成、十二階，如圓丘之制。

translations.literal: They also made a round altar below the mountain, three tiers and twelve flights, on the Round Mound model.
translations.idiomatic: Below the mountain they built a round altar of three tiers and twelve flights, following Round Mound design.

sentences.zh: 又積柴於壇南為燎壇，如山上。

translations.literal: They also piled firewood south of the altar for a burning altar, as on the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: South of that altar they likewise piled firewood for a burning altar, matching the mountaintop arrangement.

sentences.zh: 又為玉冊、玉匱、石䃭，皆如高宗之制。

translations.literal: They also made jade registers, jade caskets, and stone chests, all on Gaozong's model.
translations.idiomatic: They also fashioned jade registers, jade caskets, and stone chests, all following Gaozong's specifications.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初以謂升中於崇山，精享也，不可諠譁。

translations.literal: Xuanzong at first held that ascending the central peak for the refined offering must not be noisy.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong initially held that ascending the central peak for the refined offering must not be disturbed by clamor.

sentences.zh: 欲使亞獻已下皆行禮山下壇，召禮官講議。

translations.literal: He wished the secondary offerer and below all to perform rites at the altar below the mountain and summoned ritual officers to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: He wished the secondary and final offerers and all ranks below to perform rites at the mountain-foot altar and summoned ritual officers to debate the point.

sentences.zh: 學士賀知章等言：「昊天上帝，君也。

translations.literal: Academician He Zhizhang and others said: "August Heaven the Supreme Lord is the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Academician He Zhizhang and others said: "August Heaven the Supreme Lord is the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 五方精帝，臣也。

translations.literal: The Five Directional Essence Emperors are ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Directional Essence Emperors are ministers."

sentences.zh: 陛下享君於上，羣臣祀臣於下，可謂變禮之中。

translations.literal: Your Majesty receives the sovereign above while the ministers sacrifice to the ministers below—this may be called the middle way of changing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty receives the sovereign above while ministers sacrifice to ministers below—this may be called a measured change within ritual.

sentences.zh: 然禮成於三，亞、終之獻，不可異也。

translations.literal: Yet ritual is completed in three; the secondary and final offerings cannot differ.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ritual is completed in three stages; the secondary and final offerings cannot be separated.

sentences.zh: 」於是三獻皆升山，而五方帝及諸神皆祭山下壇。

translations.literal: " Thereupon all three offerings ascended the mountain, while the Five Emperors and other spirits were sacrificed at the altar below.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon all three offerings were performed on the mountain, while the Five Emperors and other spirits were sacrificed at the altar below.

sentences.zh: 玄宗問：「前世何為祕玉牒？

translations.literal: Xuanzong asked: "Why did former ages keep the jade tablet secret?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong asked: "Why did former ages keep the jade tablet secret?"

sentences.zh: 」知章曰：「玉牒以通意於天，前代或祈長年，希神仙，旨尚微密，故外莫知。

translations.literal: " Zhizhang said: "The jade tablet conveys intent to Heaven; former ages sometimes prayed for long life or hoped for immortals; the purpose was secret, so outsiders did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhang replied: "The jade tablet conveys one's intent to Heaven; former ages sometimes prayed for long life or sought immortality; the purpose was kept secret, so outsiders did not know."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕今為民祈福，無一祕請，即出玉牒以示百寮。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I now pray blessings for the people with no secret request; let the jade tablet be shown to the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I now pray blessings for the people with no secret request; display the jade tablet to the hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 」乃祀昊天上帝於山上壇，以高祖配。

translations.literal: " He then sacrificed to August Heaven the Supreme Lord at the mountain altar, with Gaozu as associate.
translations.idiomatic: He then sacrificed to August Heaven the Supreme Lord at the mountain altar, with Gaozu as associate.

sentences.zh: 祀五帝以下諸神於山下，其祀禮皆如圓丘。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors and spirits below were sacrificed at the foot, all sacrifices like the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors and lesser spirits were sacrificed below, all following Round Mound protocol.

sentences.zh: 而卜日、告天及廟、社、大駕所經及告至、問百年、朝覲，皆如巡狩之禮。

translations.literal: Choosing the day, announcing to Heaven and the temples, the imperial progress route, arrival announcement, inquiry into centenarians, and audience all followed tour-of-inspection ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing the day, announcing to Heaven and the temples, the imperial progress, arrival announcement, inquiry among centenarians, and court audience all followed tour-of-inspection ritual.

sentences.zh: 其登山也，為大次於中道，止休三刻而後升。

translations.literal: In ascending the mountain, a great pavilion was set on the middle path; he rested three quarters of an hour before ascending.
translations.idiomatic: For the ascent, a great pavilion was erected on the middle path; the emperor rested three quarters of an hour before continuing up.

sentences.zh: 其已祭燔燎，侍中前跪稱：「具官臣某言，請封玉冊。

translations.literal: After sacrifice and burning, the attendant director knelt forward and said: "Your subject, officer so-and-so, reports: please seal the jade register.
translations.idiomatic: After sacrifice and burning, the attendant director knelt forward and said: "Your subject, officer so-and-so, reports: we request permission to seal the jade register."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝升自南陛，北向立。

translations.literal: " The emperor ascended from the southern flight and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended from the southern flight and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 太尉進昊天上帝神座前，跪取玉冊，置於桉以進。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal advanced before August Heaven the Supreme Lord's spirit seat, knelt, took the jade register, placed it on the table, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal advanced before August Heaven the Supreme Lord's spirit seat, knelt, took the jade register, set it on the table, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受玉冊，跪內之玉匱，纏以金繩，封以金泥。

translations.literal: The emperor received the jade register, knelt, placed it inside the jade casket, bound it with gold cord, and sealed it with gold mud.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the jade register, knelt, placed it in the jade casket, bound it with gold cord, and sealed it with gold mud.

sentences.zh: 侍中取受命寶跪以進。

translations.literal: The attendant director took the Seal of Receiving the Mandate, knelt, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant director took the Seal of Receiving the Mandate, knelt, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝取寶以印玉匱，侍中受寶，以授符寶郎。

translations.literal: The emperor took the seal and stamped the jade casket; the attendant director received the seal and handed it to the Keeper of Seals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the seal and stamped the jade casket; the attendant director received the seal and passed it to the Keeper of Seals.

sentences.zh: 太尉進，皇帝跪捧玉匱授太尉，太尉退，復位。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal advanced; the emperor knelt, held out the jade casket and gave it to the Grand Marshal, who withdrew and returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal advanced; the emperor knelt, held out the jade casket and entrusted it to the Grand Marshal, who withdrew and returned to position.

sentences.zh: 太常卿前奏：「請再拜。

translations.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices stepped forward and announced: "Please bow again.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices stepped forward and announced: "Please bow again."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝再拜，退入于次。

translations.literal: " The emperor bowed again and withdrew into the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed again and withdrew into the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 太尉奉玉匱之桉於石䃭南，北向立。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal bore the jade casket's table south of the stone chest and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal bore the table with the jade casket to the south of the stone chest and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 執事者發石蓋，太尉奉玉匱，跪藏於石䃭內。

translations.literal: Attendants opened the stone lid; the Grand Marshal bore the jade casket, knelt, and stored it inside the stone chest.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants opened the stone lid; the Grand Marshal bore the jade casket, knelt, and stored it inside the stone chest.

sentences.zh: 執事者覆石蓋，檢以石檢，䃭以金繩，封以石泥，以玉寶遍印，引降復位。

translations.literal: Attendants closed the stone lid, covered with stone covers, bound the chest with gold cord, sealed with stone mud, stamped all over with the jade seal, and led the descent back to position.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants closed the lid, set the stone covers, bound the chest with gold cord, sealed it with stone mud, stamped it throughout with the jade seal, and led the party down to resume position.

sentences.zh: 帥執事者以石距封固，又以五色土圜封。

translations.literal: The commander had attendants fix it with stone distance-blocks and also seal it round with five-colored earth.
translations.idiomatic: The commander had attendants secure it with stone distance-blocks and seal it round with five-colored earth.

sentences.zh: 其配座玉牒封於金匱，皆如封玉匱。

translations.literal: Associate seats' jade tablets sealed in gold caskets all followed sealing the jade casket.
translations.idiomatic: Jade tablets for associate seats, sealed in gold caskets, followed the same procedure as the main jade casket.

sentences.zh: 太尉奉金匱從降，俱復位。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal bore the gold caskets down and all returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal bore the gold caskets down the mountain and all returned to position.

sentences.zh: 以金匱內太廟，藏於高祖神堯皇帝之石室。

translations.literal: The gold caskets were placed inside the Grand Temple and stored in the stone chamber of the High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao.
translations.idiomatic: The gold caskets were brought into the Grand Temple and stored in the stone chamber of the High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao.

sentences.zh: 其禪于社首，皆如方丘之禮。

translations.literal: The shan at Sheshou all followed Square Mound ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The shan rite at Sheshou followed Square Mound protocol throughout.

sentences.zh: 天子將巡狩，告於其方之州曰：「皇帝以某月于某巡狩，各脩乃守，考乃職事。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven was about to tour, he announced to the provinces of that direction: "The emperor in such-and-such month will tour in such-and-such place; each repair your defenses and examine your duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven prepared a tour of inspection, he announced to the provinces in that direction: "The emperor in such-and-such month will conduct a tour of inspection in such-and-such place; each of you shall repair your defenses and review your official duties.

sentences.zh: 敢不敬戒，國有常刑。

translations.literal: Dare not fail in reverent warning—the state has fixed punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Let none fail in reverent preparation—the state has fixed punishments for neglect.

sentences.zh: 」將發，告于圓丘。

translations.literal: " When about to depart, he announced at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Before departure he announced the tour at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 前一日，皇帝齋，如郊祀，告昊天上帝，又告于太廟、社稷。

translations.literal: One day before, the emperor fasted as for suburban sacrifice, announcing to August Heaven the Supreme Lord and also to the Grand Temple and Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: One day beforehand the emperor fasted as for a suburban sacrifice, announcing to August Heaven the Supreme Lord and also to the Grand Temple and the Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 具大駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: The full imperial guard of honor was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The full imperial guard of honor was made ready.

sentences.zh: 所過州、縣，刺史、令候於境，通事舍人承制問高年，祭古帝王、名臣、烈士。

translations.literal: At each province and county passed through, the prefect and magistrate waited at the border; the Master of Ceremonies, by imperial order, inquired after the aged and sacrificed to ancient emperors, famous ministers, and martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: At each province and county along the route, the prefect and magistrate waited at the border; the Master of Ceremonies, by imperial order, inquired after the aged and sacrificed to ancient emperors, famous ministers, and martyrs.

sentences.zh: 既至，刺史、令皆先奉見。

translations.literal: On arrival, the prefect and magistrate all first presented themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival, the prefect and magistrate all presented themselves first.

sentences.zh: 將作築告至圓壇於嶽下，四出陛，設昊天上帝、配帝位。

translations.literal: The Director of Palace Construction built an Arrival Announcement round altar below the peak, with steps on four sides, setting seats for August Heaven the Supreme Lord and associate lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Palace Construction built an Arrival Announcement round altar below the peak with steps on four sides, setting seats for August Heaven the Supreme Lord and the associate lords.

sentences.zh: 天子至，執事皆齋一日。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven arrived, all attendants fasted one day.
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven arrived, all officiants fasted for one day.

sentences.zh: 明日，望於嶽、鎮、海、瀆、山、川、林、澤、丘、陵、墳、衍、原、隰，所司為壇。

translations.literal: The next day he gazed in sacrifice at the peaks, commanderies, seas, rivers, mountains, streams, forests, marshes, mounds, hills, tombs, plains, highlands, and low wetlands; the responsible offices made altars.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he performed the gaze-sacrifice to peaks, commanderies, seas, rivers, mountains, streams, forests, marshes, mounds, hills, tombs, plains, highlands, and low wetlands; the responsible offices prepared altars.

sentences.zh: 設祭官次於東壝門外道南，北向；

translations.literal: Sacrifice officers' stations were set south of the eastern enclosure gate road, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice officers' stations were placed south of the eastern enclosure gate road, facing north;

sentences.zh: 設饌幔內壝東門外道北，南向；

translations.literal: food curtains were set north of the inner enclosure eastern gate road outside, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: food curtains north of the inner enclosure's eastern gate road, facing south;

sentences.zh: 設宮縣、登歌；

translations.literal: palace music and ascending song were set;
translations.idiomatic: palace music and ascending song were arranged;

sentences.zh: 為瘞埳。

translations.literal: a burial pit was made.
translations.idiomatic: a burial pit was prepared.

sentences.zh: 祭官、執事皆齋一日。

translations.literal: Sacrifice officers and attendants all fasted one day.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice officers and attendants again fasted one day.

sentences.zh: 嶽、鎮、海、瀆、山、川、林、澤、丘、陵、墳、衍、原、隰之尊，在壇上南陛之東，北向。

translations.literal: The lords of peaks, commanderies, seas, rivers, mountains, streams, forests, marshes, mounds, hills, tombs, plains, highlands, and low wetlands were east of the southern flight on the altar, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit seats for peaks, commanderies, seas, rivers, mountains, streams, forests, marshes, mounds, hills, tombs, plains, highlands, and low wetlands stood east of the altar's southern flight, facing north.

sentences.zh: 設玉篚及洗，設神坐壇上北方。

translations.literal: Jade baskets and lavation were set; spirit seats were set north on the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Jade baskets and lavation vessels were set out; spirit seats were placed on the northern part of the altar.

sentences.zh: 獻官奠玉幣及爵於嶽神，祝史助奠鎮、海以下。

translations.literal: Offering officers laid jade silks and cups before the peak spirit; invokers and recorders assisted in offering to commanderies and seas and below.
translations.idiomatic: Offering officers laid jade silks and cups before the peak spirit; invokers and recorders assisted in offerings to commandery and sea spirits and those below.

sentences.zh: 明日，乃肆覲，將作於行宮南為壝。

translations.literal: The next day came the general audience; the Director of Palace Construction made an enclosure south of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next day came the general audience; the Director of Palace Construction erected an enclosure south of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 三分壝間之二在南，為壇於北，廣九丈六尺，高九尺，四出陛。

translations.literal: Two-thirds of the space between the three enclosures was south; an altar was built in the north, nine zhang six chi wide, nine chi high, with steps on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thirds of the space between the three enclosures lay to the south; an altar was built in the north, nine zhang six chi wide and nine chi high, with steps on four sides.

sentences.zh: 設宮縣壇南，御坐壇上之北，解劍席南陛之西。

translations.literal: Palace music was set south of the altar; the imperial seat north atop the altar; sword-removal mat west of the southern flight.
translations.idiomatic: Palace music was set south of the altar; the imperial seat north atop the altar; the sword-removal mat west of the southern flight.

sentences.zh: 文、武官次門外東、西，刺史、令次文官南，蕃客次武官南，列輦路壇南。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials waited outside the gates east and west; prefects and magistrates south of civil officials; foreign guests south of military officials, lined along the imperial road south of the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials waited outside the east and west gates; prefects and magistrates south of the civil officials; foreign guests south of the military officials, lined along the imperial road south of the altar.

sentences.zh: 文官九品位壇東南，武官西南，相向。

translations.literal: Civil officials of nine ranks were southeast of the altar, military southwest, facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of nine ranks stood southeast of the altar and military officials southwest, facing each other.

sentences.zh: 刺史、令位壇南三分庭一，蕃客位於西。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates stood one-third into the courtyard south of the altar; foreign guests to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates stood one-third into the courtyard south of the altar; foreign guests to the west.

sentences.zh: 又設門外位，建牙旗於壝外，黃麾大仗屯門，鈒戟陳壝中。

translations.literal: Outside positions were also set; battle flags were raised outside the enclosure; yellow banners and great guards held the gate; halberds arrayed within the enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Outside positions were also set; battle flags were raised outside the enclosure; yellow banners and great guards held the gate; halberds arrayed within the enclosure.

sentences.zh: 吏部主客戶部贊羣官、客使就門外位。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel, Host Affairs, and Revenue guided officials and envoys to outside positions.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of the Ministries of Personnel, Host Affairs, and Revenue guided officials and envoys to their outside positions.

sentences.zh: 刺史、令贄其土之實，錦、綺、繒、布、葛、越皆五兩為束，錦以黃帊，常貢之物皆篚，其屬執列令後。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates presented the fruits of their soil; brocade, damask, silk, cloth, ramie, and fine linen were all bundled in fives of two; brocade wrapped in yellow cloth; regular tribute goods all in baskets; their subordinates carried them in column behind the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates presented the fruits of their soil; brocade, damask, silk, cloth, ramie, and fine linen were bundled in pairs of five; brocade was wrapped in yellow cloth; regular tribute goods went in baskets, carried in column behind each magistrate.

sentences.zh: 文武九品先入就位。

translations.literal: Civil and military of nine ranks entered and took position first.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of nine ranks entered first and took position.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘輿入北壝門，繇北陛升壇，即坐，南向。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the northern enclosure gate in the carriage, ascended the altar by the northern flight, took seat, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the northern enclosure gate in his carriage, ascended the altar by the northern flight, took his seat facing south.

sentences.zh: 刺史、蕃客皆入壝門，至位，再拜，奠贄，興，執贄。

translations.literal: Prefects and foreign guests all entered the enclosure gate, reached position, bowed twice, presented tribute, rose, and held the tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and foreign guests all entered the enclosure, reached position, bowed twice, presented tribute, rose, and held their offerings.

sentences.zh: 侍中降于刺史東北，皆拜。

translations.literal: The attendant director descended to the northeast of the prefect; all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant director descended to the prefect's northeast; all bowed.

sentences.zh: 宣已，又拜。

translations.literal: When the announcement was finished, they bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: When the announcement ended, they bowed again.

sentences.zh: 蕃客以舍人稱制如之。

translations.literal: Foreign guests were addressed by the Master of Ceremonies proclaiming the edict in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: For foreign guests the Master of Ceremonies proclaimed the edict in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 戶部導貢物入刺史前，龜首之，金次之，丹、漆、絲、纊四海九州之美物，重行陳。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue guided tribute goods before the prefect; tortoise led, gold next, cinnabar, lacquer, silk, and floss—the fine products of the four seas and nine provinces—arrayed in rows.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue guided tribute goods before the prefect: tortoise first, gold next, then cinnabar, lacquer, silk, and floss—the fine products of the four seas and nine provinces—arrayed in rows.

sentences.zh: 執者退，就東西文武前，側立。

translations.literal: Bearers withdrew and stood beside the civil and military officials east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers withdrew and stood beside the civil and military officials to east and west.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人導刺史一人，解劍脫舄，執贄升前，北向跪奏：「官封臣姓名等敢獻壤奠。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies guided one prefect, who removed sword and shoes, held tribute, ascended forward, knelt facing north and reported: "Your subject, officer of such-and-such seal and name, dares present soil tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies guided one prefect, who removed sword and shoes, bore tribute forward, knelt facing north, and reported: "Your subject, officer of such-and-such seal and name, dares present soil tribute."

sentences.zh: 」遂奠贄。

translations.literal: " He then presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented the tribute.

sentences.zh: 舍人跪舉以東授所司，刺史劍、舄復位。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies knelt, raised it eastward, and handed it to the responsible office; the prefect resumed sword and shoes and returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies knelt, raised the offering eastward, and handed it to the responsible office; the prefect resumed sword and shoes and returned to position.

sentences.zh: 初，刺史升奠贄，在庭者以次奠於位前，皆再拜。

translations.literal: At first, when the prefect ascended to present tribute, those in the courtyard presented in turn before their positions, all bowing twice.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefect ascended to present tribute, those in the courtyard presented in turn before their positions, each bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書壇間北向跪，請以貢物付所司，侍中承制曰：「可。

translations.literal: The Minister of Revenue knelt between the altars facing north and requested that tribute goods be handed to the responsible office; the attendant director, by edict, said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Revenue knelt between the altars facing north and requested that tribute goods be handed to the responsible office; the attendant director, by edict, said: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 」所司受贄出東門。

translations.literal: " The responsible office received tribute and went out the eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office received the tribute and went out the eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎以州鎮表方一桉俟于西門外，給事中以瑞桉俟于東門外，乃就侍臣位。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Secretariat waited with the provincial tables and maps on one table outside the western gate; the Supervising Censor waited with the auspicious table outside the eastern gate; then they took positions among attendant ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director of the Secretariat waited with provincial tables and maps on one table outside the western gate; the Supervising Censor waited with the auspicious table outside the eastern gate; then both took positions among the attendant ministers.

sentences.zh: 初，刺史將入，乃各引桉分進東、西陛下。

translations.literal: At first, when the prefect was about to enter, each drew his table and advanced separately on the eastern and western flights.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefect was about to enter, each drew his table and advanced separately on the eastern and western flights.

sentences.zh: 刺史將升，中書令、黃門侍郎降立，既升，乃取表升。

translations.literal: When the prefect was about to ascend, the Secretariat Director and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate descended and stood; after he ascended, they took the table and ascended.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefect was about to ascend, the Secretariat Director and Vice Director of the Yellow Gate descended and stood; after he ascended, they took the table and ascended.

sentences.zh: 尚書既請受贄，中書令乃前跪讀，黃門侍郎、給事中進跪奏瑞，侍郎、給事中導桉退，文武、刺史、國客皆再拜。

translations.literal: After the Minister had requested to receive tribute, the Secretariat Director knelt forward and read; the Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Supervising Censor advanced, knelt, and reported the auspicious message; the Vice Director and Supervising Censor guided the tables down; civil and military officials, prefects, and foreign guests all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: After the Minister requested to receive tribute, the Secretariat Director knelt forward and read; the Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Supervising Censor advanced, knelt, and reported the auspicious message; the Vice Director and Supervising Censor guided the tables down; civil and military officials, prefects, and foreign guests all bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 北向位者出就門外位。

translations.literal: Those in northern positions went out to outside positions.
translations.idiomatic: Those in northern positions went out to their outside positions.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降北陛以入，東、西位者出。

translations.literal: The emperor descended the northern flight to enter; those in east and west positions went out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended the northern flight to enter; those in east and west positions departed.

sentences.zh: 設會如正、至，刺史、蕃客入門，皆奏樂如上公。

translations.literal: A banquet was set like the winter and summer solstices; prefects and foreign guests entered the gate, all with music as for a chief duke.
translations.idiomatic: A banquet was arranged like the solstice feasts; prefects and foreign guests entered the gate, all with music as for a chief duke.

sentences.zh: 會之明日，考制度。

translations.literal: The day after the banquet, institutions were examined.
translations.idiomatic: The day after the banquet, local institutions were examined.

sentences.zh: 太常卿採詩陳之，以觀風俗。

translations.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices collected songs and presented them to observe customs.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices collected songs and presented them to observe local customs.

sentences.zh: 命市納賈，以觀民之好惡。

translations.literal: The market was ordered to receive merchants to observe the people's likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: The market was ordered to receive merchants so the people's likes and dislikes could be observed.

sentences.zh: 典禮者考時定日，同律，禮、樂、制度、衣服正之。

translations.literal: Those in charge of ritual examined the seasons and fixed days, harmonized laws, and corrected ritual, music, institutions, and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers examined the seasons and fixed days, harmonized laws, and corrected ritual, music, institutions, and clothing.

sentences.zh: 山川神祇有不舉為不恭，宗廟有不慎為不孝，皆黜爵。

translations.literal: If mountains, rivers, and spirits were not sacrificed to, it was disrespect; if the ancestral temples were not tended, it was unfilial—both were punished by removal of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Failure to sacrifice to mountains, rivers, and spirits was deemed disrespect; careless tending of ancestral temples was deemed unfilial—both were punished by removal of rank.

sentences.zh: 革制度、衣服者為叛，有討。

translations.literal: Those who altered institutions and clothing were rebels and were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who altered institutions and clothing were deemed rebels and were subject to punitive action.

sentences.zh: 有功德於百姓者，爵賞之。

translations.literal: Those with merit for the hundred surnames were ennobled and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Those with merit on behalf of the common people were ennobled and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 皇帝視學，設大次于學堂後，皇太子次于大次東。

translations.literal: When the emperor inspected the schools, a great pavilion was set behind the academy hall; the crown prince's pavilion was east of the great pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor inspected the schools, a great pavilion was set behind the academy hall and the crown prince's pavilion east of it.

sentences.zh: 設御座堂上，講榻北向。

translations.literal: The imperial seat was set in the hall; the lecture couch faced north.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial seat was placed in the hall; the lecture couch faced north.

sentences.zh: 皇太子座御座東南，西向。

translations.literal: The crown prince's seat was southeast of the imperial seat, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's seat lay southeast of the imperial seat, facing west.

sentences.zh: 文臣三品以上座太子南，少退；

translations.literal: Civil officials of third rank and above sat south of the crown prince, slightly withdrawn;
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of third rank and above sat south of the crown prince, slightly withdrawn;

sentences.zh: 武臣三品以上於講榻西南；

translations.literal: military officials of third rank and above southwest of the lecture couch;
translations.idiomatic: military officials of third rank and above southwest of the lecture couch;

sentences.zh: 執讀座於前楹，北向。

translations.literal: the reader's seat at the front pillar, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: the reader's seat at the front pillar, facing north.

sentences.zh: 侍講座執讀者西北、武官之前；

translations.literal: The lecture attendant's seat northwest of the reader, before the military officials;
translations.idiomatic: The lecture attendant's seat lay northwest of the reader, before the military officials;

sentences.zh: 論義座於講榻前，北向。

translations.literal: the discourse seat before the lecture couch, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: the discourse seat before the lecture couch, facing north.

sentences.zh: 執如意立於侍講之東，北向。

translations.literal: One holding the ruyi scepter stood east of the lecture attendant, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: One holding the ruyi scepter stood east of the lecture attendant, facing north.

sentences.zh: 三館學官座武官後。

translations.literal: Academy officials of the Three Halls sat behind the military officials.
translations.idiomatic: Academy officials of the Three Halls sat behind the military officials.

sentences.zh: 設堂下版位，脫履席西階下。

translations.literal: Courtyard positions were set; shoe-removal mats below the western flight.
translations.idiomatic: Courtyard positions were set; shoe-removal mats below the western flight.

sentences.zh: 皇太子位於東階東南，執經於西階西南，文、武三品以上分位於南，執如意者一人在執經者後，學生位于文、武後。

translations.literal: The crown prince stood southeast of the eastern flight; the scripture-holder southwest of the western flight; civil and military of third rank and above divided positions to the south; one ruyi-holder behind the scripture-holder; students behind civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince stood southeast of the eastern flight; the scripture-holder southwest of the western flight; civil and military officials of third rank and above took divided positions to the south; one ruyi-holder behind the scripture-holder; students behind the civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 其日，皇帝乘馬，祭酒帥監官、學生迎于道左。

translations.literal: On that day the emperor rode a horse; the libationer led supervising officers and students to welcome on the road's left.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the emperor rode; the libationer led supervising officers and students to welcome him on the left of the road.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入次，執經、侍講、執如意者與文武、學生皆就位堂下。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the pavilion; scripture-holder, lecture attendant, ruyi-holder, with civil, military, and students all took courtyard positions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the pavilion; the scripture-holder, lecture attendant, and ruyi-holder, with civil and military officials and students, all took courtyard positions.

sentences.zh: 皇太子立于學堂門外，西向。

translations.literal: The crown prince stood outside the academy gate, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince stood outside the academy gate, facing west.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: The attendant director reported "outer preparations complete."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant director reported, "Outer preparations are complete."

sentences.zh: 皇帝升北階，即坐。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the northern flight and took seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the northern flight and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 皇太子乃入就位，在位皆再拜。

translations.literal: The crown prince then entered and took position; all in position bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince then entered and took position; all present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 侍中敕皇太子、王公升，皆再拜，乃坐。

translations.literal: The attendant director ordered the crown prince and princes to ascend; all bowed twice, then sat.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant director ordered the crown prince and princes to ascend; all bowed twice, then sat.

sentences.zh: 執讀、執經釋義。

translations.literal: The reader and scripture-holder expounded the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The reader and scripture-holder expounded the text.

sentences.zh: 執如意者以授侍講，秉詣論義坐，問所疑，退，以如意授執者，還坐，乃皆降。

translations.literal: The ruyi-holder gave it to the lecture attendant, who went bearing it to the discourse seat, asked what was doubtful, withdrew, gave the ruyi back to the holder, returned to seat, and all descended.
translations.idiomatic: The ruyi-holder passed it to the lecture attendant, who bore it to the discourse seat, raised questions, withdrew, returned the ruyi to the holder, resumed his seat, and all descended.

sentences.zh: 若賜會，則侍中宣制，皇帝返次。

translations.literal: If a banquet was granted, the attendant director proclaimed the edict and the emperor returned to the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: If a banquet was granted, the attendant director proclaimed the edict and the emperor returned to the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 羣官既會，皇帝還，監官、學生辭於道左。

translations.literal: After the officials had met, the emperor returned; supervising officers and students took leave on the road's left.
translations.idiomatic: After the officials had assembled, the emperor returned; supervising officers and students took leave on the left of the road.

sentences.zh: 皇帝孟春吉亥享先農，遂以耕藉。

translations.literal: On the auspicious hai day of the first month the emperor enjoyed sacrifice to the First Farmer, then performed plowing the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On the auspicious hai day of the first month the emperor sacrificed to the First Farmer, then performed plowing of the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 前享一日，奉禮設御坐於壇東，西向；

translations.literal: One day before the enjoyment, the Director of Ritual set the imperial seat east of the altar, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: One day before the sacrifice, the Director of Ritual set the imperial seat east of the altar, facing west;

sentences.zh: 望瘞位於壇西南，北向；

translations.literal: the gaze-burial position southwest of the altar, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: the gaze-burial position southwest of the altar, facing north;

sentences.zh: 從官位於內壝東門之內道南，執事者居後；

translations.literal: attendant officials inside the eastern enclosure gate on the road south; attendants behind;
translations.idiomatic: attendant officials inside the eastern enclosure gate on the road south, with attendants behind;

sentences.zh: 奉禮位於樂縣東北，贊者在南。

translations.literal: the Director of Ritual northeast of the music stand; presenters south.
translations.idiomatic: the Director of Ritual northeast of the music stand; presenters to the south.

sentences.zh: 又設御耕藉位於外壝南門之外十步所，南向；

translations.literal: They also set the imperial plowing position ten paces outside the southern outer enclosure gate, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: They also set the imperial plowing position ten paces outside the southern outer enclosure gate, facing south;

sentences.zh: 從耕三公、諸王、尚書、卿位於御坐東南，重行西向，以其推數為列。

translations.literal: the Three Dukes, princes, ministers, and directors who joined the plowing southeast of the imperial seat, in double rows facing west, ranked by number of furrows.
translations.idiomatic: the Three Dukes, princes, ministers, and directors who joined the plowing southeast of the imperial seat, in double rows facing west, ranked by number of furrows pushed.

sentences.zh: 其三公、諸王、尚書、卿等非耕者位於耕者之東，重行，西向北上；

translations.literal: The Three Dukes, princes, ministers, and directors who did not plow stood east of the plowers, in double rows facing west and advancing north;
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes, princes, ministers, and directors who did not plow stood east of the plowers in double rows, facing west as they advanced north;

sentences.zh: 介公、酅公於御位西南，東向北上。

translations.literal: the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Xi southwest of the imperial position, facing east and advancing north.
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Xi southwest of the imperial position, facing east and advancing north.

sentences.zh: 尚舍設御耒席於三公之北少西，南向。

translations.literal: The Palace Provisioner set the imperial plow mat north and slightly west of the Three Dukes, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Provisioner set the imperial plow mat north and slightly west of the Three Dukes, facing south.

sentences.zh: 奉禮又設司農卿之位於南，少退；

translations.literal: The Director of Ritual also set the Director of Agriculture's position to the south, slightly withdrawn;
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ritual also set the Director of Agriculture's position to the south, slightly withdrawn;

sentences.zh: 諸執耒耜者位於公卿耕者之後、非耕者之前，西向。

translations.literal: those holding plow and hoe behind the dukes' and directors' plowers and before the non-plowers, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: those holding plow and hoe behind the dukes' and directors' plowers and before the non-plowers, facing west.

sentences.zh: 御耒耜一具，三公耒耜三具，諸王、尚書、卿各三人合耒耜九具。

translations.literal: One imperial plow set; three plow sets for the Three Dukes; nine combined plow sets for princes, ministers, and directors, three persons each.
translations.idiomatic: One imperial plow; three plow sets for the Three Dukes; nine combined plow sets for princes, ministers, and directors, three persons each.

sentences.zh: 以下耒耜，太常各令藉田農人執之。

translations.literal: Below that, plows and hoes—the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had the sacred-field farmers hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Lower ranks used plows and hoes—the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had sacred-field farmers hold them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝已享，乃以耕根車載耒耜於御者間，皇帝乘車自行宮降大次。

translations.literal: After the emperor had enjoyed sacrifice, he then used the Root-Plowing carriage to load plow and hoe between the drivers; the emperor rode from the traveling palace down to the great pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice, the Root-Plowing carriage loaded plow and hoe between the drivers; the emperor rode from the traveling palace down to the great pavilion.

sentences.zh: 乘黃令以耒耜授廩犧令，橫執之，左耜寘於席，遂守之。

translations.literal: The Yellow Carriage Office gave plow and hoe to the Director of Granaries and Sacrificial Animals, who bore them crosswise, left share set on the mat, and guarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Carriage Office handed plow and hoe to the Director of Granaries and Sacrificial Animals, who bore them crosswise, set the left share on the mat, and guarded them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝將望瘞，謁者引三公及從耕侍耕者、司農卿與執耒耜者皆就位。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to gaze at the burial, ushers led the Three Dukes, attendant plowers, the Director of Agriculture, and plow-holders all to position.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to perform the gaze-burial, ushers led the Three Dukes, attendant plowers, the Director of Agriculture, and plow-holders all to position.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出就耕位，南向立。

translations.literal: The emperor went out to the plowing position and stood facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went out to the plowing position and stood facing south.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令進耒席南，北向，解韜出耒，執以興，少退，北向立。

translations.literal: The Director of Granaries advanced south of the plow mat, facing north, removed the cover and brought out the plow, bore it raised, withdrew slightly, and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Granaries advanced south of the plow mat, facing north, removed the cover, brought out the plow, bore it raised, withdrew slightly, and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 司農卿進受之，以授侍中，奉以進。

translations.literal: The Director of Agriculture advanced, received it, and gave it to the attendant director, who bore it forward.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Agriculture advanced, received it, and gave it to the attendant director, who bore it forward.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受之，耕三推。

translations.literal: The emperor received it and plowed three furrows.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received it and plowed three furrows.

sentences.zh: 侍中前受耒耜，反之司農卿，卿反之廩犧令，令復耒於韜，執以興，復位。

translations.literal: The attendant director advanced, received plow and hoe, returned them to the Director of Agriculture, who returned them to the Director of Granaries; he replaced the plow in the cover, bore it raised, and returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant director advanced, received plow and hoe, returned them to the Director of Agriculture, who returned them to the Director of Granaries; he replaced the plow in the cover, bore it raised, and returned to position.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初耕，執耒者皆以耒耜授侍耕者。

translations.literal: When the emperor first plowed, all plow-holders gave plow and hoe to the attendant plowers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first plowed, all plow-holders handed plow and hoe to the attendant plowers.

sentences.zh: 皇帝耕止，三公、諸王耕五推，尚書、卿九推。

translations.literal: When the emperor stopped plowing, the Three Dukes and princes plowed five furrows and ministers and directors nine.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor stopped, the Three Dukes and princes plowed five furrows and ministers and directors nine.

sentences.zh: 執耒者前受之。

translations.literal: The plow-holders advanced and received them.
translations.idiomatic: The plow-holders stepped forward to receive them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝還，入自南門，出內壝東門，入大次。

translations.literal: The emperor returned, entered by the southern gate, went out the inner eastern enclosure gate, and entered the great pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned, entered by the southern gate, went out the inner eastern enclosure gate, and entered the great pavilion.

sentences.zh: 享官、從享者出，太常卿帥其屬耕于千畝。

translations.literal: Sacrifice officers and participants went out; the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led his subordinates to plow the thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice officers and participants departed; the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led his subordinates to plow the thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 皇帝還宮，明日，班勞酒於太極殿，如元會，不賀，不為壽。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to the palace; the next day he distributed reward wine at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, like the New Year assembly but without congratulations or longevity wishes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the palace; the next day reward wine was distributed at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, as at the New Year assembly but without congratulations or longevity wishes.

sentences.zh: 藉田之穀，斂而鍾之神倉，以擬粢盛及五齊、三酒，穰槀以食牲。

translations.literal: The grain of the sacred field was gathered and stored in the Spirit Granary to supply sacrificial grain and the five clears and three wines, with straw fodder to feed the sacrificial animals.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from the sacred field was gathered into the Spirit Granary to supply sacrificial grain, the five clears and three wines, and straw fodder for sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 藉田祭先農，唐初為帝社，亦曰藉田壇。

translations.literal: The sacred-field sacrifice to the First Farmer—in early Tang was the Emperor's Altar of Soil, also called the Sacred Field Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the First Farmer at the sacred field—in early Tang this was the Emperor's Altar of Soil, also called the Sacred Field Altar.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，太宗將親耕，給事中孔穎達議曰：「禮，天子藉田南郊，諸侯東郊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, when Taizong was about to plow in person, Remonstrance Grandee Kong Yingda argued: "The Rites say the Son of Heaven plows the sacred field at the southern suburb and feudal lords at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan, as Taizong prepared to plow in person, Remonstrance Grandee Kong Yingda argued: "The Rites say the Son of Heaven plows the sacred field at the southern suburb and feudal lords at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝猶東南，今帝社乃東壇，未合於古。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin still used the southeast; now the Emperor's Altar is an eastern altar, not in accord with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin still used the southeast; now the Emperor's Altar is an eastern altar, which does not match antiquity.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「書稱『平秩東作』，而青輅、黛耜，順春氣也。

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "The Documents say 'rank the eastern work,' and the green carriage and dark plow follow spring's qi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied: "The Documents speak of 'ranking the eastern work,' and the green carriage and dark plow follow spring's vital force.

sentences.zh: 吾方位少陽，田宜于東郊。

translations.literal: My position is lesser yang; the field should be in the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: My position is lesser yang; the field belongs in the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 」乃耕于東郊。

translations.literal: " He then plowed in the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: He then plowed in the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，武后藉田壇曰先農壇。

translations.literal: In the Zhongguan era, Empress Wu's sacred-field altar was named the First Farmer Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhongguan era, Empress Wu renamed the sacred-field altar the First Farmer Altar.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，禮部尚書祝欽明議曰：「周頌載芟：『春藉田而祈社稷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming argued: "The Zhou Odes' Praise of the Harvests: 'In spring plow the sacred field and pray to the Altars of Soil and Grain.'
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, Minister of Rites Zhu Qinming argued: "The Zhou Odes' Praise of the Harvests reads: 'In spring plow the sacred field and pray to the Altars of Soil and Grain.'

sentences.zh: 』禮：『天子為藉千畝，諸侯百畝。

translations.literal: The Rites: 'The Son of Heaven makes a thousand mu for the sacred field; feudal lords a hundred mu.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites state: 'The Son of Heaven makes a thousand mu for the sacred field; feudal lords a hundred mu.'

sentences.zh: 』則緣田為社，曰王社、侯社。

translations.literal: Hence along the field one establishes the altars called King's Altar and Marquis's Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Hence along the field one establishes altars called the King's Altar and the Marquis's Altar.

sentences.zh: 今曰先農，失王社之義，宜正名為帝社。

translations.literal: Now it is called First Farmer, losing the meaning of the King's Altar; the name should be corrected to Emperor's Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Calling it First Farmer loses the meaning of the King's Altar; the name should be corrected to Emperor's Altar.

sentences.zh: 」太常少卿韋叔夏、博士張齊賢等議曰：「祭法，王者立太社，然後立王社，所置之地，則無傳也。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Shuxia and Erudite Zhang Qixian and others argued: "The Sacrificial Canon says the king first establishes the Grand Altar of Soil, then the King's Altar; where they are placed has no transmitted record.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Shuxia and Erudite Zhang Qixian argued: "The Sacrificial Canon says the king first establishes the Grand Altar of Soil, then the King's Altar; where they were placed has no transmitted record.

sentences.zh: 漢興已有官社，未立官稷，乃立于官社之後，以夏禹配官社，以后稷配官稷。

translations.literal: When Han arose there was already an official altar of soil but no official altar of grain; one was then set behind the official altar of soil, with Yu of Xia as associate for the official altar of soil and Hou Ji for the official altar of grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose there was already an official altar of soil but no official altar of grain; one was then set behind the official altar of soil, with Yu of Xia as associate for the official altar of soil and Hou Ji for the official altar of grain.

sentences.zh: 臣瓚曰：『高紀，立漢社稷，所謂太社也。

translations.literal: Chen Zan says: 'In the Annals of Gaozu, the Han altars of soil and grain were established—this is the Grand Altar of Soil.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zan says: 'In the Annals of Gaozu, the Han altars of soil and grain were established—this is the Grand Altar of Soil.

sentences.zh: 官社配以禹，所謂王社也。

translations.literal: The official altar of soil with Yu as associate is the so-called King's Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The official altar of soil with Yu as associate is the so-called King's Altar.

sentences.zh: 至光武乃不立官稷，相承至今。

translations.literal: By Emperor Guangwu the official altar of grain was no longer established, handed down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Guangwu the official altar of grain was no longer established, and that practice continued thereafter.

sentences.zh: 』魏以官社為帝社，故摯虞謂魏氏故事立太社是也。

translations.literal: Wei took the official altar of soil as the Emperor's Altar; hence Zhi Yu said Wei's precedent of establishing the Grand Altar of Soil was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took the official altar of soil as the Emperor's Altar; hence Zhi Yu said Wei's precedent of establishing the Grand Altar of Soil was correct.

sentences.zh: 晉或廢或置，皆無處所。

translations.literal: Under Jin it was sometimes abolished and sometimes established, all without fixed location.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin it was sometimes abolished and sometimes established, always without a fixed location.

sentences.zh: 或曰二社並處，而王社居西。

translations.literal: Some say the two altars stood together, with the King's Altar to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the two altars stood together, with the King's Altar to the west.

sentences.zh: 崔氏、皇甫氏皆曰王社在藉田。

translations.literal: Master Cui and Master Huangfu both say the King's Altar was at the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: Master Cui and Master Huangfu both say the King's Altar was at the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 桉衞宏漢儀『春始東耕於藉田，引詩先農，則神農也。

translations.literal: Examining Wei Hong's Han Rites: 'At spring's start plow east at the sacred field; citing the Odes' First Farmer, that is Shennong.'
translations.idiomatic: Examining Wei Hong's Han Rites: 'At spring's start plow east at the sacred field; citing the Odes' First Farmer—that is Shennong.'

sentences.zh: 』又五經要義曰：『壇於田，以祀先農如社。

translations.literal: The Essentials of the Five Classics also says: 'An altar in the field to sacrifice to the First Farmer like an altar of soil.'
translations.idiomatic: The Essentials of the Five Classics also says: 'An altar in the field to sacrifice to the First Farmer like an altar of soil.'

sentences.zh: 』魏秦靜議風伯、雨師、靈星、先農、社、稷為國六神。

translations.literal: Wei Qin Jing argued that Wind Lord, Rain Master, Spirit Star, First Farmer, altars of soil and grain were the six spirits of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qin Jing argued that Wind Lord, Rain Master, Spirit Star, First Farmer, and the altars of soil and grain were the six spirits of the state.

sentences.zh: 晉太始四年，耕於東郊，以太牢祀先農。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi under Jin, plowing at the eastern suburb sacrificed to the First Farmer with the great offering.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin's fourth year of Taishi, plowing at the eastern suburb sacrificed to the First Farmer with the great offering.

sentences.zh: 周、隋舊儀及國朝先農皆祭神農于帝社，配以后稷。

translations.literal: Zhou and Sui old rites and the present dynasty's First Farmer all sacrificed to Shennong at the Emperor's Altar of Soil, with Hou Ji as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Sui old rites and the present dynasty's First Farmer all sacrificed to Shennong at the Emperor's Altar of Soil, with Hou Ji as associate.

sentences.zh: 則王社、先農不可一也。

translations.literal: Thus the King's Altar and First Farmer cannot be one.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the King's Altar and First Farmer could not be one and the same.

sentences.zh: 今宜於藉田立帝社、帝稷，配以禹、棄，則先農、帝社並祠，叶於周之載芟之義。

translations.literal: Now one should establish Emperor's Altar of Soil and Emperor's Altar of Grain at the sacred field, with Yu and Qi as associates; then First Farmer and Emperor's Altar would be sacrificed together, matching the Zhou meaning of Praise of the Harvests.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed establishing Emperor's Altar of Soil and Emperor's Altar of Grain at the sacred field, with Yu and Qi as associates, so First Farmer and Emperor's Altar could be sacrificed together, matching the Zhou meaning of Praise of the Harvests.

sentences.zh: 」欽明又議曰：「藉田之祭本王社。

translations.literal: Qinming again argued: "Sacrifice at the sacred field is originally the King's Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming argued again: "Sacrifice at the sacred field is originally the King's Altar.

sentences.zh: 古之祀先農，句龍、后稷也。

translations.literal: In antiquity sacrifice to the First Farmer was to Goulong and Hou Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity sacrifice to the First Farmer honored Goulong and Hou Ji.

sentences.zh: 烈山之子亦謂之農，而周棄繼之，皆祀為稷。

translations.literal: The son of Lieshan was also called Farmer; Zhou Qi succeeded him; both were sacrificed as grain lords.
translations.idiomatic: The son of Lieshan was also called Farmer; Zhou Qi succeeded him; both were worshipped as lords of grain.

sentences.zh: 共工之子曰后土，湯勝夏，欲遷而不可。

translations.literal: The son of Gonggong was called Lord of Soil; when Tang overcame Xia, he wished to move him but could not.
translations.idiomatic: The son of Gonggong was called Lord of Soil; when Tang overcame Xia, he wished to move him but could not.

sentences.zh: 故二神，社、稷主也。

translations.literal: Hence the two spirits are lords of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the two spirits are lords of the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 黃帝以降，不以羲、農列常祀，豈社、稷而祭神農乎？

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor down, Xi and Nong were not listed in regular sacrifice—how sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain and yet sacrifice to Shennong?
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor down, Xi and Nong were not listed in regular sacrifice—how could one sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain and yet sacrifice to Shennong?

sentences.zh: 社、稷之祭，不取神農耒耜大功，而專於共工、烈山，蓋以三皇洪荒之迹，無取為教。
